pro_course_detail.title: Sound like a Native with the American English Mouth Posture!
pro_course_detail.description:
READ FIRST: I only accept serious students who will make time outside of class and put in the work required. I will guide you and give you the tools and techniques you need, but your results are mostly dependent on you. This isn't a traditional class where you show up, do a few exercises, and then forget about it until the next lesson.

OUTLINE

We're changing the SETTINGS of how you hold the vocal tract underneath the sounds, meaning that it's less about producing certain sounds (which will also be covered) and more about maintaining the correct settings at all times. That's the main thing that creates the accent, not the sounds.

This course has a few phases:

Phase 0: You'll become aware of your tongue and overall vocal tract, as well as your native posture. If needed, this will include special exercises designed to help you get better control over different parts of the tongue and throat. Phase 0 overlaps with phase 1.


Phase 1: We'll use the House Framework to build the core of the American posture, the foundation for everything else. This includes the schwa/UH/center of gravity. We'll also start working on breathing.


Phase 2: We'll use various techniques and exercises as we go through 2 sections to build the sounds with the posture and slowly start linking things together into syllables, words, and sentences. We'll also add linking, stress, etc as we go, but these are not a main focus in the beginning. 99% of people underestimate the work we're doing and want to jump right to words and sentences, but that's exactly the same as trying to run when you haven't learned to walk.

-SECTION 1 SOUNDS (mostly front):
T/D/N, S/Z, K/G/NG, AW (cot/caught), Y, EE, IH, EH, AH (cat), EI, AI

-SECTION 2 SOUNDS (mostly lips and back): F/V, P/B/M, SH/ZH, CH/J, TH/TH, W, U, O, UUH (book), OW, OI


Phase 3 (new centers of gravity): R (both + R-colored), L (both + L-colored). The R and dark L (mostly) take over the center of gravity and also "color"/blend with various sounds.

pro_course_detail.title: General Pronunciation Lessons (NOT Mouth Posture Course)
pro_course_detail.description:
This class is for anyone who wants to work on their American accent WITHOUT mouth posture. It is NOT possible to have a perfect accent without mouth posture. In addition, the mouth posture approach also makes things easier overall (though it might seem harder in the short term). However, if you just want to sound better/clearer (not perfect or near perfect) and/or you just want to improve certain areas of pronunciation such as stress or linking, then this class is for you. However, I do NOT teach advanced intonation. Basic intonation patterns are fine, but advanced intonation is a tricky topic that I dislike teaching. The exact content we focus on can be tailored to your needs, goals, and interests.

Note that the mouth posture class contains all areas of pronunciation, but things like stress, linking, and rhythm come little by little as we move through the course and are not the main focus, especially in the beginning. Please see the mouth posture course for more information. It is STRONGLY recommended that you at least learn the basic components of mouth posture because it helps everything else, especially the formation and clarity of individual sounds (and will also improve your listening indirectly). We can include these basics in this class if desired.

We can also do any ear training you might need, including hearing the difference between certain sounds, properly hearing the stress, and more.

1-hour classes at least twice a week is recommended, but not required.

Lastly, I do NOT teach beginners. You must have at least a B1/lower-intermediate level. B2/upper-intermediate is preferred. For B1 and B2 students (especially B1), these classes will also drastically improve your listening skills.

course_info.trial_description:
Welcome to Your Personalized Trial Lesson!

Are you ready to take your language skills to the next level? In this 30-minute trial lesson, we will work together to create a learning experience that is uniquely tailored to your goals. Whether you're learning for travel, business, exams, or just personal enrichment, this session is the perfect starting point to help you reach your objectives.

Here’s what you can expect:

Introduction (5-10 minutes):
We’ll start by getting to know each other. I’ll ask a few questions about your language learning background and your goals. This will help me understand your current level, any challenges you’ve been facing, and what areas you would like to improve. By taking this time to learn about your unique situation, I can personalize the rest of the lesson to suit your needs.
Mini-Lesson (15-20 minutes):
This part of the lesson is where we’ll dive into a short, engaging activity based on your goals. If you’re focusing on conversation skills, we’ll have a dialogue where I’ll correct your grammar, pronunciation, and fluency. If you need help with grammar, we’ll go through an easy-to-understand explanation, followed by practical exercises. For those preparing for exams, I can provide tips and sample exercises to build your confidence. Regardless of the focus, you’ll experience a hands-on, interactive lesson designed to boost your language abilities.
Feedback and Future Plan (5 minutes):
At the end of the trial lesson, I’ll give you specific feedback on your strengths and areas for improvement. We’ll talk about the next steps in your learning journey and how I can help you achieve your goals. You’ll leave the lesson with a clear understanding of what you need to work on and a customized plan for future lessons with me.

pro_course_detail.title: Basic English with Conversation
pro_course_detail.description:
This lesson is perfect for beginners or intermediate learners who want to improve their everyday conversation skills. We’ll focus on practical, real-life situations to help you speak more confidently and naturally. I recommend the 30 minute option if your budget is tight. We can do a lot in 30 minutes!

What We’ll Cover:

Talking About Your Day – Start by discussing your daily routine. You’ll learn how to describe your activities and add details to keep the conversation going.
Conversation Starters – Practice essential phrases for small talk, like discussing the weather, hobbies, or recent events.
Expressing Opinions – Learn how to share your thoughts and feelings effectively in simple, natural sentences.
Listening Skills – We’ll also work on responding to others’ comments and keeping the conversation flowing.
Lesson Structure:

Warm-Up (10 minutes): We’ll begin by chatting about your day to help you relax and ease into speaking.
Main Practice (30 minutes): We’ll dive into basic conversation topics. I’ll guide you through speaking exercises, offer corrections, and help you expand your answers to sound more natural.
Feedback & Next Steps (10 minutes): I’ll provide feedback on areas to improve and tips for continuing your practice after the lesson.
Why This Lesson?

If you want to feel more comfortable speaking in everyday situations, this lesson will help. We’ll focus on boosting your fluency, improving your vocabulary, and getting you more confident in conversation. No need to worry about mistakes—I’m here to help you speak with ease and confidence!

Join this Basic Conversation lesson to build your speaking skills and gain confidence in day-to-day interactions. Let's get started on your path to fluency!

pro_course_detail.title: Intermediate English with Conversation
pro_course_detail.description:
Are you ready to take your conversational skills to the next level? This Intermediate Conversation lesson is designed to help you become more confident and fluent in your speaking abilities. Whether you're looking to improve your daily communication, prepare for travel, or engage in deeper discussions on a variety of topics, this course is perfect for those who already have a basic understanding of the language and want to advance.

What You’ll Get:
Real-life Conversations: We'll focus on practical, real-world topics that are relevant to your interests and goals. These conversations will challenge you to use your vocabulary and grammar in ways that feel natural.
Fluency & Pronunciation: You’ll work on improving your fluency by speaking more naturally, practicing pronunciation, and picking up useful phrases that native speakers use in everyday interactions.
Cultural Insights: Learn not just the language but also the culture behind it. I’ll guide you through idioms, colloquial expressions, and cultural contexts that will enhance your understanding and ability to communicate with native speakers.
Customizable Lessons: I tailor each lesson to your specific needs. Whether you want to focus on work-related conversations, social interactions, or just building overall confidence, we’ll design the conversation topics that suit your learning goals.
Feedback & Corrections: At the end of each session, I’ll provide constructive feedback, focusing on areas for improvement like grammar, vocabulary usage, and fluency. You'll also receive suggestions on how to continue practicing outside of class.
Who Should Join:
Intermediate Learners: If you can hold basic conversations but find it hard to express complex thoughts, this course is for you.
Improving Everyday Communication: Great for learners who want to enhance their ability to have casual and formal conversations with native speakers.

pro_course_detail.title: Advanced/Business English

Are you looking to improve your English communication skills for a professional environment? This Business English course is tailored for individuals who need to develop their language skills to succeed in international business settings. Whether you're preparing for job interviews, meetings, presentations, or just want to enhance your overall business communication, this course will help you reach your goals.

What You’ll Learn:
Business Vocabulary: We’ll cover the essential vocabulary you need for different business situations, including meetings, negotiations, presentations, and emails. You’ll learn phrases and terminology that are common in professional environments.
Fluent Communication: We’ll focus on improving your ability to speak clearly and effectively in business contexts. You’ll practice both formal and informal business communication to ensure you’re ready for a variety of situations.
Email Writing & Reports: Learn how to write professional emails and reports with clarity and precision. We’ll cover key strategies for effective written communication, including how to organize your ideas and avoid common mistakes.
Presentations & Public Speaking: Gain confidence in delivering presentations and speaking in front of others. You’ll practice organizing your thoughts, speaking clearly, and engaging your audience to deliver persuasive presentations.
Meetings & Negotiations: Whether you need to chair a meeting or participate in discussions, we’ll practice real-life scenarios to help you improve your ability to contribute to business conversations. You’ll learn how to express your opinions, agree or disagree professionally, and negotiate effectively.
Cultural Awareness: In international business, understanding cultural differences is key. I’ll help you navigate these differences so that you can communicate respectfully and effectively with colleagues and clients from diverse backgrounds.

Professionals & Job Seekers

pro_course_detail.title: The Sound of American English (Accent Reducction)
pro_course_detail.description:
Do you want to master the unique sound of American English? In this course, The Sound of American English, we’ll dive deep into the specific sounds, rhythms, and intonations that define the American accent. Whether you're just beginning or looking to refine your existing skills, this course will help you speak with clarity and confidence, allowing you to sound more natural in conversations.

What You’ll Learn:
Distinct American Sounds: American English has its own set of vowels and consonants that are pronounced differently compared to other accents. We’ll work on these unique sounds, including the "r-colored" vowels, the flat "a," and others, to help you master the authentic American sound.
Rhythm and Intonation: American English is known for its rhythm and melody, with natural rises and falls in speech. You’ll learn to use intonation patterns that native speakers rely on to convey meaning, emotion, and emphasis.
Word Stress and Syllable Emphasis: Pronunciation is also about where you place the stress in a word. We’ll practice how to correctly stress syllables and words, which is key to sounding fluent and avoiding misunderstandings.
Common American Pronunciation Patterns: Many words in American English are shortened or connected in casual speech. We’ll explore these patterns, such as word linking and reductions (e.g., "gonna," "wanna"), to make your pronunciation more conversational and less formal.
Accent Reduction Techniques: If you’re looking to reduce your accent and adopt a more American sound, we’ll focus on techniques to help you speak more like a native. From practicing subtle changes in vowel and consonant sounds to perfecting rhythm and tone, you’ll learn how to sound more natural in American English.
Listening and Mimicking: A key part of learning pronunciation is listening to how native speakers talk.
